cultural.vision_reason: Silver overlay brooch made and signed by a Hopi artist, depicting Kokopolmana against a pueblo motif in classic Hopi silver overlay technique — directly matches the claimed ethnicity.

physical.title: brooch
physical.summary: Brooch of overlay technique depicting female flute player Kokopolmana (mana= girl in Hopi) against background of adobe houses. The background is oxidized and scored to produce the relief effect. The design is contemporary and ceremonial events. She is portrayed as rather lascivious a role she enacts in Night Dances in March/April in Hopi villages. The Brooch has a sterling pin with a safety catch. The piece is signed, the makers mark seems to be a tablita.

cultural.vision_reason: Silver overlay pendant depicting a Long Haired Kachina figure, a classic Hopi silversmithing technique and iconography attributed directly to a Hopi maker.

physical.title: pendant
physical.summary: Silver pendant, overlay technique, depicting Long Haired Kachina. The Long Haired Kachina is made up of rain symbols: the beard is a storm pattern, the arm a rain cloud, the lower part of the body a wave/cloud/rain, the bottom of the pendant is an inverted rain cloud. The shape is a thin tapering rectangle with a stepped edge at the bottom and a loop soldered back on itself. The overlay is raised. The silver sheet underneath is oxidised and scored to create the hair effect. The makers mark is a face with a beard.
